newsitem.title: UK: Sugar freight market sees wave of fresh inquiry.
newsitem.headline: Sugar freight market sees wave of fresh inquiry.

text.p: The sugar freight market started the week with a spate of fresh inquiry from a variety of quoted origins, shipbrokers said on Monday.
Iran again proved popular as a destination, reflecting its recent spate of physical buying of both white and raw sugar from Europe and Cuba.
E D & F Man quoted for 13,300/14,700 tonnes min/max preslung bagged sugar from north Spain to Iran for 20/30 March. At least two other account orders were noted.
UBC was open on account for a 14,000-tonne bagged order from Continent to Iran for 5/15 April, suggesting rates at around $38 for the cargo.
Ceba Shipping quoted an unnamed account order for the same amount for 1/15 April with 10 days notice to Iran from the EU excluding the UK.
Andre's recent order for 26,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Cuba to Iran for end March/early April was thought to remain unfilled.

Shipbrokers said the freight market was still reflecting Iraqi offtake, albeit in limited quantities. Shyvers Savoy quoted for 12,000 tonnes of bagged sugar on account from Goa to Umm Qasr for 1/10 April.

The only reported fixture to emerge on Monday came from CSR, believed to have fixed 26,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Queensland to China for end March/early April. Details of the rate have yet to emerge.

E D & F Man repeated its Guatemala and Thailand inquiries and Genoc was still open with its order for 14,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Poland to north Africa with options of Red Sea, Pakistan and Bangladesh.

Pacol quoted for 25,000 tonnes of Cuban bulk sugar to Black Sea for prompt dates and Louis Dreyfus was in for a same-sized cargo from the Philippines to the US Gulf, east or west coasts for prompt dates.

The only Brazilian order came from an unnamed UK charterer or nominee quoted by the Anglo-Caribbean Shipping Company, open for 12,500 tonnes in bags from Paranagua to Dar es Salaam for prompt or later dates.

Sucre Export was thought to be in the market with two Calais bagged orders for end March/early April, quoting for 12/13,000 tonnes to Algeria with origin option of Antwerp and 13/13,500 tonnes to Med/Black Sea.
Czarnikow Rionda was open with two bagged orders specifying Africa as a destination.

It quoted for 8,500/9,000 tonnes from Mazatlan/Manzanillo to west/east Africa for 20 March/10 April and 12/14,000 tonnes from east coast Mexico to west Africa/Mediterranean/east Africa for 25 March/10 April.
Kerry Foodstuffs quoted for 6/10,000 tonnes min/max in bags from Thailand to Indonesia for prompt/seven days and another prompt 3/3,500 tonnes on the same run.
Naeco was still open with its bagged order from south China but quoted for 15/20,000 tonnes in bulk from Puerto Quetzal to Puerto Cabello or Maracaibo for May dates.
Cargill was open with two Thailand orders, quoting for 10,000 tonnes in bulk to Kunsan for 5/10 April and 12,500/14,200 tonnes bulk/bagged to Indonesia or the Philippines for the end of March.
David Bruce quoted an account order for 16/24,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Puerto Quetzal to Toronto for 27 March/April 15.

NST was open on account for 10,800/12,000 tonnes in bags from south China to Pakistan/Red Sea for 25 March onwards but preferring 26/27 March arrival. It noted that the last rate was $21 basis Pakistan and $22 for Red Sea.

D.K. Shipping issued an unnamed account order to ship 12,500 tonnes of bagged sugar in 50 kg bags from Mexico's Californian Gulf port of Topolobampo to Dubai for 17/22 April, suggesting a rate arounf $50 for the order.
Seven Seas was looking for tonnage to cover 2,600 tonnes in bags to go from Port Sudan to Aqaba for !9 March/onwards, with the possibility of a further order for 3,700 tonnes to Aden.
In other news, the Cyprus-flagged bulk carrier Theodoros S. and the Turkey-registered Gulsum Ana were in collision 30 miles off Malaga, according to a report from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence.
The Theodoros S., 27,023 dwt and carrying a cargo of sugar, was holed and being towed to Cadiz for repairs while the Gulsum Ana was only slightly damaged and had made its own way to Malaga, it said.
-- Jeremy Smith, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8064
